old_problem: The H.265 title names encoding, while Procedure names only playback/visual inspection and Criteria is TBD. In addition, the next independent Source Key is labeled HEVC—the same codec family—with materially identical body and timing. disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending, Source Conflict and BLOCKED. Official NVIDIA and FFmpeg sources establish that HEVC/H.265 NVENC encoding, NVDEC decoding and physical display are separate paths and that `libx265` is software, not GPU evidence. ED-21 resolves one governance question: Wistron-HW-00414-V002 and the adjacent HEVC case must remain independently identifiable and separately executable/verifiable even if text overlaps; they cannot be merged, deleted or passed by one shared result. ED-21 does not decide this row's intended pipeline or distinct profile/bit-depth/resolution/workload, and it does not replace the TBD oracle. Those are core operation and acceptance gaps, so a fresh owner ruling remains necessary.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1781, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 conflict/blocked record, pending/conflict/blocked analyses, exact-code and adjacent HEVC comparison, ED-01 through ED-30 including case-specific ED-21, and official codec documentation were read. The next formal identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1782 / Wistron-HW-00415-V002 / de65b63c40585598.

H.265 and HEVC are names for the same codec family; naming alone supplies no distinct coverage. ED-21 nevertheless requires both Source Keys and their own execution/evidence identities to remain, so this review neither de-duplicates nor borrows a future HEVC result.

Items and Procedure still conflict within this row: hardware encoding generates a bitstream, while playback/visual output requires decoding and scanout. NVIDIA documents NVENC and NVDEC as separate engines, and clean pixels cannot prove encoding.

FFmpeg documents `libx265` as the software x265 wrapper and `hevc_nvenc` as the NVIDIA hardware encoder with GPU/driver/build-dependent capabilities. DeepSeek's CPU-to-null example is neither H.265 GPU proof nor retained media evidence.

HEVC profiles, levels, 8/10-bit depth, chroma, resolution, frame rate, rate control, GOP and reference/quality materially change coverage. The owner must assign this identity a specific stage/profile/workload or other unique purpose without using the adjacent case as a substitute.

`bleeding edge` and Criteria TBD supply no objective visual oracle. A golden/reference frame set plus approved metric/tolerance or a precise operator artifact checklist must be provided; no threshold is inferred.
No ffmpeg, NVENC, NVDEC, media write, playback, visual inspection, log clear or DUT action was executed.
